About: Reading x–t, v–t and a–t Graphs

Source

Topic
Kinematics in one dimension — motion graphs
Simulation
Trolley on a track with linked x–t, v–t and a–t plots
Concept
The slope of one motion graph is the height of the next — three plots, one motion differentiated twice.
Serves
Reading graphs; distinguishing speeding up from a positive acceleration; distinguishing displacement from distance.
Inquiry
With v₀ > 0 and a < 0, where on the x–t curve is the trolley momentarily at rest?
Misconception
“Positive acceleration means speeding up.” Not so — when v and a have opposite signs, the body slows down and reverses.

Guided Inquiry

1 · Predict — where does it stop?

Set the initial velocity positive and the acceleration negative (the defaults do this: v₀ = 4 m/s, a = −1 m/s²). The trolley starts moving right while being pushed left. On the x–t curve, where is it momentarily at rest?

2 · Watch — the three curves are one motion

Press ▶ Play (or drag the time cursor by clicking on the graphs). Watch the vertical cursor cross all three plots at once. As the trolley slows, the tangent on x–t flattens, the v–t line marches down to zero, and a–t stays flat and negative.

Notice the shaded area under v–t: green above the axis (positive displacement) and pink below (negative). The displacement readout is that signed sum.

3 · The misconception

Now think about the sign of the acceleration versus what the trolley is doing. Which statement is correct?

4 · Displacement vs distance

After the trolley turns around, the total distance travelled and the net displacement stop being equal — a second readout (“distance”) appears once the trolley has passed its turning point. Distance is the sum of |v|·dt; displacement is the sum of v·dt with signs.

Try v₀ = 3, a = −1.5, then pause and drag the cursor to t = 5 s: displacement reads −3.75 m (behind the start) while distance keeps growing.

5 · Explore

Two sliders, both signed. Try:

• v₀ = 2, a = 0.75 — same sign, always speeding up, x–t curls upward.
• v₀ = 4, a = −1 — opposite signs, one turning point at t = 4 s.
• v₀ = 0, a > 0 — starts from rest, x–t is a pure parabola.

Changing a slider redraws all three curves at once for the new v₀ and a, so each curve you see is a single, honest solution.

Motion Graphs

✦Learn this with the AI tutor

01

At a glance

A trolley moves along a straight track while three graphs are drawn from the same motion: where it is, how fast it goes, and how its velocity changes. Reading the three together turns lines on a page into a description of what the trolley is doing.

What you'll learn

  • How to read position, velocity and acceleration from graphs against time.
  • How the three graphs of one motion are linked to each other.
  • How to tell speeding up from slowing down on the graphs.
  • The difference between displacement and distance travelled.
One trolley with a starting velocity v₀ and an acceleration a, and the three graphs against time t.

What's on screen

  • Track: a side view with a −25 m to +25 m scale, a dashed line at x = 0, the trolley (drawn as a small car), a green arrow for its velocity and a pink arrow for its acceleration.
  • Three graphs: x–t (blue), v–t (green) and a–t (pink), stacked, sharing one time axis from 0 to 8 s.
  • Time cursor: an amber line through all three graphs, with a dot on each curve.
  • At the cursor panel: v and x at the cursor time.
See itRun the trolley with v₀ = +4 m/s and a = −1 m/s². Watch for: the amber cursor sweeping across all three graphs while the trolley moves on the track.

03

The slope of each graph is the height of the next

Velocity is how fast position changes, so v is the slope of the x–t graph. Acceleration is how fast velocity changes, so a is the slope of the v–t graph. The dashed amber line on x–t is the tangent at the cursor, and its slope is the v readout. For a constant acceleration a:

x = v₀t + ½at²
v = v₀ + at
v is the slope of x, and a is the slope of v.

So x–t is a parabola, v–t is a straight line with slope a, and a–t is a flat line at height a. A flat a–t line says the v–t line is equally steep everywhere.

See itRun the default motion and follow the dashed tangent on x–t. Watch for: the tangent flattening toward t = 4 s, then tilting downward, while the v–t line falls and a–t stays at −1.
04

At a turning point the velocity is zero

When v₀ and a have opposite signs, the trolley slows, stops for an instant and then reverses. Setting v = v₀ + at to zero gives the time of the stop:

tturn = −v₀ / a
Only if this time falls inside the 0 to 8 s window.

On x–t this is the peak (or the trough), where the tangent is flat. With v₀ = +4 m/s and a = −1 m/s², the stop is at t = 4 s and x = 8 m. Notice that a is still −1 m/s² at that instant: only v is zero, and the v–t line keeps falling straight through the axis.

v₀ a

These sliders move the sim too.

See itPut the cursor at t = 4 s on the default motion. Watch for: v reading +0.00 m/s and x reading +8.00 m, with the tangent flat at the top of x–t.
05

The signs of v and a together decide the speed

The speed |v| grows when v and a have the same sign, and shrinks when they have opposite signs. The sign of a alone does not say which. In the default run, a stays at −1 m/s² the whole time:

  • From 0 to 4 s, v is positive and a is negative, so the trolley slows down.
  • After 4 s, v is negative and a is negative, so it speeds up while moving left.
  • At t = 6 s, v = −2.00 m/s and x = +6.00 m: the trolley is heading back toward the start, and getting faster.

The car drawn in the sim shows its brake lights while v and a oppose.

See itPut the cursor at t = 6 s on the default motion. Watch for: v reading −2.00 m/s while a is still −1, with the v–t curve below its axis.
06

Displacement is a signed area, distance is not

The area between the v–t curve and the axis, from 0 to t, is the displacement. Area above the axis (green in the sim) counts as positive, and area below it (pink) as negative. Distance travelled adds every area as positive. In the same way, the area under a–t is the change in velocity, Δv = at.

Take v₀ = +3 m/s and a = −1.5 m/s². The trolley turns at t = 2 s, having gone +3 m. By t = 5 s it has gone back 6.75 m, so:

Quantity at t = 5 sSumResult
displacement x+3 − 6.75−3.75 m
distance travelled3 + 6.759.75 m
See itSet v₀ = +3 and a = −1.5, and put the cursor at t = 5 s. Watch for: x = −3.75 m and a third row, distance travelled, reading 9.75 m.
07

Reading the shapes of the curves

The shape of x–t tells you the signs of v₀ and a at a glance.

  • Same signs (v₀ = +2 m/s, a = +0.75 m/s²): the trolley never turns. x–t curls steadily upward, and by 8 s it is at x = 40 m, well past the ±25 m track view.
  • Opposite signs (the default): x–t rises, peaks and falls back. Here it ends at x = 0 at t = 8 s, although 16 m of track have been covered.
  • Starting from rest (v₀ = 0, a > 0): x–t leaves the origin flat and bends upward, a pure parabola.
  • Zero acceleration (a = 0): v–t is flat and x–t is a straight line.
See itRun v₀ = +2 m/s with a = +0.75 m/s². Watch for: x–t curling upward with no peak, v–t rising, and a caption on the track once x passes 25 m.
08

Where it matters

  • A ball thrown upward. Taking up as positive, it has v₀ > 0 and a = −g, about −9.8 m/s². The graphs have the same shapes as the default run, with the turning point at the top of the flight. The sim's slider stops at −2 m/s², so it shows the same shape at a smaller rate.
  • Speed-time graphs. A car's log of speed against time gives its distance as the area under the curve and its acceleration as the slope.
  • A lift. Its v–t graph has sloped ends, where it speeds up and slows down, and a flat middle at constant speed, where a = 0.
  • The limit. The formulas on this sheet need a constant a. With a changing a, the slope and area rules still hold, but the curves are no longer a parabola and a straight line.
09

Summary

In one line. One motion at constant acceleration is drawn as three linked graphs, and each can be read from the others.

Key points

  • The slope of x–t is v, and the slope of v–t is a.
  • The signed area under v–t is the displacement, and under a–t it is Δv.
  • With v₀ and a of opposite signs, the trolley stops at t = −v₀/a.
  • Speed grows when v and a share a sign, and falls when they oppose.

Common mix-ups

  • "A positive acceleration means speeding up." It depends on v as well. With v negative and a positive, the trolley slows down.
  • "When v = 0, then a = 0." At the turning point v is zero but a is not. The v–t line is still sloping.
  • "Distance is the displacement without its sign." Only before the turn. After it, distance adds the outward and return legs, so it is larger than |x|.

Things to try on your own

  • Set v₀ = +6 and a = −2, then move the cursor to the stop and compare it with −v₀/a.
  • With v₀ = 0 and a = +1, read x at t = 2 s and t = 4 s, and compare the two.
  • Find two different pairs of v₀ and a that bring the trolley back to x = 0 at t = 8 s, and note how v₀ and a are related.
